thread:
ashley: Quick perms check — planning to give analytics team access to export project logs to BigQuery. If we grant `roles/editor` at project scope, do they get access to secrets surfaced in logs (e.g., KMS-encrypted fields or PII)? Looking for least-privilege path.

jamal: Don't give Editor. Editor is broad and will allow changes to KMS keys and other resources. For log exports you only need logging sink & dataset-level perms, not project-level Editor.

sasha: For a BigQuery export you need `roles/logging.configWriter` to create the sink (project-level) and the sink's service account needs `roles/bigquery.dataEditor` on the destination dataset. Analysts querying the dataset need separate BQ roles — don't hand out Editor.

jamal: Also watch for sensitive fields in logs. Exporting raw logs to BQ can surface PII. We should either exclude sensitive log paths with a sink filter or redact at ingestion. Important: `bigquery.dataEditor` does NOT grant KMS decrypt unless the dataset uses CMEK and the SA has encrypter/decrypter on the key.

ashley: Cool. So recommended minimal set for an analytics workflow that needs exports + queries?

jamal: Minimal: 1) Grant a small group `roles/logging.configWriter` (or one service account) to create the sink. 2) Create a dedicated dataset for log exports. 3) Give the sink SA `roles/bigquery.dataEditor` on that dataset. 4) For analysts, grant `roles/bigquery.dataViewer` or a custom dataset-level role. Avoid project-level Editor/Owner. Use temporary grants for ad-hoc needs.

sasha: If they need scheduled transformations, give `roles/bigquery.jobUser` to run jobs and grant write on target dataset only. Alternatively run scheduled queries via a dedicated service account with narrow dataset perms.

ashley: How do I quickly check who's got what right now?

jamal: Quick commands: 
```
gcloud logging sinks list --project=redwood-prod
gcloud logging sinks describe my-sink --project=redwood-prod
gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-prod --flatten="bindings[]" --format='table(bindings.role, bindings.members)'
```
I'll also run a mapping to show sink SAs -> dataset ACLs and paste findings.

ashley: If logs contain KMS-encrypted blobs, could analysts decrypt them by virtue of BQ perms?

jamal: Not unless they also have KMS decrypt on that key. Decrypt requires `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` on the key. So ensure keys used for sensitive fields are tightly scoped. If the dataset is using CMEK, check the key IAM.

sasha: We should add a short runbook: 1) Create filter/exclusion for sensitive log entries, 2) Create sink to dedicated dataset, 3) Apply dataset-level roles, 4) Use temporary access and ticketing. I'll open a PR with a custom role template for dataset viewers + a sample sink creation script. :thumbsup:

ashley: Can someone approve temporary elevated access for @data-ops for 48h while they onboard queries? I'll file an access request.

jamal: Fine to approve after the runbook steps are followed and you attach the ticket ID. Keep duration explicit and add justification.

securitybot: Reminder: Any project-level IAM grants must reference an internal ticket ID per policy PRIV-23 and include expiry. See https://internal.redwood/policies/PRIV-23

ashley: Thanks all — will update the ticket and ping once PR is up.
